chapter: Opening, arrival in Los Angeles and the Quality Four
title: His father, a strictly classical cornetist
summary: Howard says his father played cornet, strictly classical music, and was angry that his son did not follow that path.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh, classics. So what about your move to, say, the Los Angeles area? About how old were you then, when you came to Los Angeles?
When I came to Los Angeles? I was
trying to think. Wait a minute. I'm trying to think, Buddy, how old I was. Let me see. Well, --
So why don't we go back to the coronet, and things that you can remember -- see, that's an instrument that --
-- the favorite (Inaudible) instrument to a lot of us.
Oh, yeah, well, it was a good one to me, and I had to play at a -- what do you call that, I had to -- kind of forget what -- oh, boy. Well, anyhow, I had the coronet.
Uh-huh. So you mentioned, too, or someone did, that your father was a coronetist?
Yeah, my father was a coronetist.
And did he play in some of the jazz bands, too?
Oh, no, he didn't play in the jazz bands. He played strictly classical music, and got mad at me because I wasn't playing it.
